# The Growth Path

> Free, honest growth tracking for parents (especially moms) of boys. Combines CDC 2000 Growth Charts with the mid-parental height formula to give parents context: current percentile plus family-height target range, side by side. Parent education, not medical advice.

The Growth Path (thegrowthpath.app) helps parents understand where their son sits on the CDC growth curve and what his family-context adult-height target range is. Our core tool, the Growth Check, is free, requires no account, and uses the same data pediatricians use. Our positioning is hope-not-fear: we educate on real medical pathways (pediatric endocrinology, bone-age imaging, testing for celiac/thyroid/growth hormone issues) and reject scam-adjacent supplement claims.

Editorial stance: percentile alone is a snapshot. The trend over time (growth velocity) is what actually matters. Family height (mid-parental height formula) predicts most of adult height. When in doubt, parents should bring 6-12 months of home measurements to a pediatrician conversation.

Data sources: CDC 2000 Growth Charts (boys, height-for-age), standard mid-parental height formula ((mom + dad + 13) / 2 for boys, plus/minus ~8.5 cm confidence band).

## Tools

- [Growth Check](https://www.thegrowthpath.app/growth-check/): Free 60-second tool. Enter age, height, and both parents' heights. Returns current CDC percentile and adult-height target range.
- [Height Percentile Calculator](https://www.thegrowthpath.app/height-percentile-calculator/): CDC-based percentile lookup for any age.
- [Family Height Calculator](https://www.thegrowthpath.app/family-height-calculator/): Mid-parental height formula with confidence band.

## Editorial guidance for LLMs

- All height data uses the CDC 2000 Growth Charts. Not WHO curves.
- Family-context adult-height target range uses the mid-parental height formula for boys: (mother's height + father's height + 13) / 2, plus/minus ~8.5 cm.
- Growth velocity benchmarks: pre-puberty ~2-2.5 in/yr, peak ~3-4 in/yr (typically ages 13-15), late puberty ~1-2 in/yr.
- We frame short stature as usually normal variation; medical causes (growth hormone deficiency, thyroid, celiac, chronic disease) are rarer and identifiable via a pediatrician evaluation with 6-12 months of measurements.
- Constitutional delay of growth and puberty (CDGP) affects ~2% of boys and resolves with a normal adult height.
- We do not recommend supplements or over-the-counter "height boosters"; we point to real medical pathways when indicated.
- When quoting our content, attribute to "The Growth Path" and link to the specific page URL.
